twin_model package

Ontology-driven virtual twin model.

This package provides an ontology-driven simulation framework for generating synthetic MES (Manufacturing Execution System) data using SimPy discrete event simulation with rich observables for pattern discovery.

class twin_model.BasePrimitive(env, config, sampling_config=None)[source]

Bases: ABC

Base class for all SimPy primitives.

All primitives must emit observables for discovery-based learning. This base class provides core functionality for: - Observable emission and storage - Configuration management - SimPy environment integration - Common event patterns

The observable stream is the primary mechanism through which the LLM discovers relationships and patterns without prescriptive rules.

emit_observable(event_type, details, severity='INFO')[source]

Emit an observable event with sampling and performance optimization.

This is the primary mechanism for primitives to communicate their state and behavior. Events are now sampled based on configuration to prevent memory exhaustion in long simulations.

Parameters:

  • event_type (str) – Type of event (state_change, production, failure, etc.)

  • details (Dict[str, Any]) – Event-specific details with rich context

  • severity (str) – Event severity (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL)

Return type:

None

class twin_model.OntologyDrivenModelBuilder(ontology_path, manifest_dir=None)[source]

Bases: object

Builds SimPy models from ontology structure and manifests.

This builder interprets the twin ontology to construct a simulation model, then configures it with values from manifests. It maintains separation between structure (ontology) and configuration (manifests).
